[00:43] Tom Bender: On pricing, can you clarify how the dedicated commit vs hosted pricing works? whose logos are used and how the credit is split?
[00:52] Liam Ortiz: I'll follow up with the commercial template. short answer: dedicated is a reserved GPU commit that we price separately; typically Meridian and Redwood agree on a referral and co-sell commission structure per opportunity  we can share examples.
[01:05] Jonas Meyer: ok that's helpful. let's run through the three opportunities  RetailCo POC (high priority), FinServe renewal (mid), LogiChain demo (discovery). RetailCo wants on-prem style controls and low latency, so they're leaning to dedicated or private.
[01:24] Priya Raman: Right  for low latency and strict data residency, Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) are the paths. quick question Maya  do you know if RetailCo requires an air-gapped on-prem install or just VPC in their cloud?
[01:38] Maya Singh: They said VPC first, but if that doesn't meet their compliance they'd consider an on-prem package. they also asked about KMS integration for key management.
[01:48] Priya Raman: Good. we can do KMS integrations  our Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs, and Dedicated can be configured with VPC peering in many cases.
[01:58] Sara Lopez: Are there SOC 2 or ISO artifacts we can share ahead of the exec call? they want security evidence before committing to a pilot.
[02:06] Alex Chen: Yes  we'll share SOC 2 Type II report, a security whitepaper, and the network architecture diagrams. I'll put that in the shared folder.
[02:14] Tom Bender: Great. for the POC scope  RetailCo wants to validate latency at 128 tokens and 512 tokens and throughput at 200 concurrent sessions  is that doable?
[02:25] Priya Raman: Yep that's within typical test parameters. we'll run a benchmark on Redwood Dedicated with their prompt set. question on model choice  do they have a preferred model or are they open to Redwood's recommended variants?
[02:36] Jonas Meyer: They prefer a Llama2-style open model, but are open to alternatives if latency/cost improves.
[02:41] Priya Raman: ok will include a 7B and a 13B quantized run in the benchmark. we'll capture latency P95, cost per 1k tokens, and failure rates.
[02:51] Jonas Meyer: Perfect. next, FinServe renewal  they want a price reduction and better forecasting. any levers you recommend?
[02:59] Liam Ortiz: we can look at longer reserved commitments for Dedicated which drive unit cost down, and also model quantization and batching profiles to hit cost targets. also Redwood Optimize can provide suggestions to reduce token spend.
[03:13] Sara Lopez: For the co-sell motion, Meridian needs an intro email template and a joint slide for the deck. Can you provide a one-pager?
[03:21] Alex Chen: Yes  Liam will own the one-pager and the deck slide. we'll share as soon as possible.
[03:26] [03:26] Maya Singh: quick technical question  if we deploy Dedicated in a region close to RetailCo, does Redwood handle kernel selection and runtime optimizations automatically? some of our customers worry about manual tuning.
[03:40] Priya Raman: yes, the runtime selects compiled kernels and handles batching and KV cache, and we have auto-tuning heuristics. sometimes we do small manual tweaks for edge cases but generally it is automatic. note: transcription may show 'kernal' sometimes in docs  that's fine.
[03:56] Tom Bender: There was also a question on fallback  if Dedicated saturates, can requests fail over to hosted models?
[04:03] Alex Chen: We support smart routing and automated fallback to compatible variants  e.g., if Dedicated is constrained, traffic can be routed to a hosted instance with a compatible model and lower SLA. that helps avoid total outage.
[04:18] Jonas Meyer: Good to know. For the benchmark, what's the expected timeline from data to results?
[04:24] Priya Raman: If we get the dataset access this week, we can run benchmark and have results in ~5 business days. that includes setup, runs at multiple seq lengths, and a write-up.
[04:35] Sara Lopez: Let's plan for that. Maya will share sample prompt sets and test data by 2025-08-07.
[04:42] Maya Singh: yep I'll put it in the shared S3 and send access.

[05:00] Liam Ortiz: also worth mentioning is lead registration  helps protect Meridian's sourced deals. we'll include that in the checklist.
[05:08] Jonas Meyer: okay, moving on to LogiChain  currently discovery, needs a demo around chain-of-thought and structured outputs. Is Redwood supportive of function/tool-calling patterns?
[05:19] Priya Raman: yes  we support streaming responses, function calling, structured output, and tool invocation patterns. we can demo a small integration during the next joint call.
[05:28] Tom Bender: For demos, do you have reference infra for performance numbers we can share with customers?
[05:34] Alex Chen: We have verified model performance profiles in our model catalog and internal benchmark sheets. we'll share a trimmed sheet that fits Meridian's use cases.
[05:43] [05:43] Jonas Meyer: any competitive risks we should be aware of? I heard Cohere is pitching a managed endpoint; Anthropic on safety.

[06:18] Maya Singh: ok that's good.
